papers.title: A Robust Reversible Watermarking Scheme Using Attack-Simulation-Based Adaptive Normalization and Embedding
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
limitations: Final TIFS 19 (2024), pages 4114-4129; no diffusion regeneration evaluation.
No operational false-attribution calibration or human study identified.
Author notes iterative embedding cost and imperfect transfer to unknown attacks.

papers.title: Instance-Level Multi-Watermark Embedding with Mask-gated Adapter against Partial Screen-shooting
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
limitations: Inspected 16-page accepted author version; final volume and page range unknown.
Detector uses pretrained instance segmentation and capture comparisons use manual perspective correction.
No operational false-attribution calibration, human study or diffusion regeneration evidence identified.
Disjoint instance masks; partial fragments and background-only captures can fail.

evidence.claim: Tang compares five external RRW methods using separate 1000-image BOWS2 comparison data and 256/512-bit payloads.
evidence.locator: IV-A, IV-E; pp.4121-4127, Tables I-II, X-XV
limitations: Image selection random seeds not established; not a diffusion test.

evidence.claim: Tang reports mean RRW-PCET PSNR40.25dB before reversible embedding and39.09dB final.
limitations: Mean image quality is not an all-source quality guarantee.

evidence.claim: Chen evaluates four external named methods and an adapted FPSMark variant on real screen captures, COCO groups and LVIS transfer.
limitations: 100 images per COCO group,50 per LVIS instance-count subset; unique aggregate and subset overlaps unknown.
Image-level methods are mask-adapted; capture images manually perspective corrected.

evidence.claim: Chen reports five-instance quality36.00dB PSNR and.964 SSIM and explicitly acknowledges failures on fragments and absence of object instances.
limitations: Bit extraction ACC does not establish false-attribution probability.

evidence.claim: These TIFS precedents support task-specific operating conditions, meaningful component ablations and quality/payload-matched comparisons as useful design targets.
evidence.locator: II-V, especially IV-C/E; synthesis also compares Chen2026Instance IV
limitations: Observed precedents cannot establish necessary or sufficient journal acceptance criteria.
assumptions: These two distinct image-watermark studies are useful but incomplete publication-bar samples.

open_questions: Whether code releases exist outside inspected author records remains unknown.
Current TIFS acceptance cannot be predicted from the sampled precedents.
